A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show that the RNA binding protein MCPIP1, which is known to cleave target mRNAs, can also act on the translational machinery.
MCPIP1 can be considered as an RNA-binding protein, which can suppress translation in the context of an mRNA target structure.
the TSE of the NFKBZ mRNA is an RNA element in the 3'UTR of the mRNA which contains a sequence that is recognized by MCPIP1/REGNASE-1.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the same RNA binding protein can perform different functions depending on the target RNA structure.
MCPIP1 is an important regulator of gene expression, which is not only involved in mRNA degradation but also in translational silencing.
